Donald Trump will reportedly not attend ceremonies commemorating the 25th anniversary of the September 11, 2001 terror attacks at Ground Zero in New York. The President - a native New Yorker who launched his real estate empire in the Big Apple - has frequently been seen at 9/11 memorials in the years since the attack. However, in 2026, he will mourn the victims for a second consecutive year in a ceremony at the Pentagon because he has not been allowed to give a speech, The New York Times reported. Trump wanted to give remarks at The National September 11 Memorial and Museum and had even gotten his team to make advance visits. But multiple sources said that the museum's ultimate goal is to avoid any partisanship at the ceremonies, with politicians banned from speaking since 2012. Vice President JD Vance will represent the Trump administration at the New York ceremony instead, while ex-Presidents Bill Clinton, Barack Obama and George W Bush are expected to attend. 📷 MLB / Getty Images #trump #yankees #mets #nyc #news
